statement.p: Calculate the integral below by partial fractions and by using the indicated substitution. Be sure that you can show how the results you obtain are the same. \int \frac{2x}{x^{2}-49}\,dx
First, rewrite this with partial fractions:

p.em: (Note that you should not include the +C in your entered answer, as it has been provided at the end of the expression.)

statement.p: Next, use the substitution w = x^2 - 49 to find the integral:

p.em: (For the second answer blank, give your antiderivative in terms of the variable w. Again, note that you should not include the +C in your answer.)

static.solution:
\frac{2x}{x^2-49}=\frac{A}{x+7}+\frac{B}{x-7} so that 2x = A(x-7)+B(x+7) = (A+B)x + 7 (-A+B). Solving, we get A=B=1, so that \int \frac{2x}{x^2-49}\,dx= \int \left(\frac{1}{x+7}+\frac{1}{x-7}\right)\,dx =\ln|x+7|+\ln|x-7|+C.
Using the substitution w=x^2-49, we get dw= 2x\,dx, so we have \int \frac{2x}{x^2-49}\,dx= \int \frac{dw}{w}=\ln|w|+C = \ln|x^2-49|+C.
The properties of logarithms show that the two results are the same: \ln|x+7|+\ln|x-7| = \ln|(x+7)(x-7)| =\ln|x^2-49|.
